newsitem.title: USA: Ford may appeal $11.9 million jury award.
newsitem.headline: Ford may appeal $11.9 million jury award.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. said Thursday it may appeal an $11.9 million award by a Baltimore jury that found alleged defects in a 1987 F-150 Ford pickup truck caused the driver to be severely burned.
"Ford strongly disagrees there is a product defect," said Ford spokesman Jon Harmon. "We are investigating whether we will appeal or not," he said by telephone from Ford's headquarters in Michigan.

Joseph Wasilik was injured in mid-February, while driving a Ford-150 pickup truck that was struck by another vehicle, according to Ford. He was trapped in the truck for several minutes and severely burned.

"Wasilik sustained tragic and terrible injuries in an accident that was not his fault. The facts of the case show that the crash clearly was caused by the negligence of another driver, a co-defendant in the trial, who crossed the centre line into Wasilik's lane," Ford said in a statement.
The jury reached its verdict on Wednesday.
